decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: measure first (the replay over the clone's check state, replies and event logs) before the rules
decisions.why: Measurement before a rule is how the GM asked for this work to go (the convergence talk opens 'let's talk about that before we do literally anything else'). The replay's arithmetic holds (115+103+499+829=1546; 35+34+31+11+2+2=115; 17+8=25; 115-31=84), and it is labeled as a floor with its date and method.

decisions.summary: T188: the category rule applies per EDIT, not per reply. In a mixed round the wording EDITs (and GLOSSARY) go first, fingerprints are read (mid), then the factual ones. Only a unit that wording alone moved settles
decisions.why: This carries 'only factual findings cascade' as stated: a unit that a factual EDIT moved still re-owes. A per-reply rule would either skip factual changes or re-owe wording, and both would break the GM's rule.

decisions.summary: T188: an EDIT whose check or category is not given is factual, and a reply naming no check settles as before
decisions.why: A fail-safe default: a mislabel costs a round and never skips a factual review, which keeps what the GM's rule protects (factual inaccuracies still cascade).

decisions.summary: T188: the wording classes (never re-owe): modal-form, record-format (VOCABULARY, SESSION NOTE, HISTORY), record-style, intro-check
decisions.why: These are the GM's 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies'. modal-form's contract already says a replacement only rewords, and the others are presentation or the order of words. A claim that one of them changes is not part of this table: it is factual by the untold/factual side, and each check's own contract binds it.

decisions.summary: T188: a modal-depiction LINKS EDIT (a pointer to a drawing page) is wording and does not cascade
decisions.why: Judged on its own, apart from the style checks. The GM's own words on splits cover it: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page ... nothing needs to cascade'. A pointer to a drawing states no fact. What a statement rests on (REFERENCES) and what a drawing shows (COVERAGE, TRUTH) stay factual, so the seam is drawn on the fact line.

decisions.summary: T188: factual (may cascade): modal-research ACCURACY/REFERENCES/GAPS, modal-depiction COVERAGE/TRUTH, quote-check, source-reader, translation-check, entry-drift
decisions.why: These are the 'factual inaccuracies' the GM said cascading is for. Putting GAPS (a statement added) on the factual side is conservative.

decisions.summary: T188: quote-check's units stay on settle_quotes, which re-owes a unit whose quoted words changed, whoever changed them (a wording EDIT included)
decisions.why: A wording EDIT can still re-owe quote-check here, so this is a carve-out from 'wording never re-owes'. It is implied by the GM's own approved sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review': changed quoted words change the claim about what a source says, which is a factual matter. A unit whose quoted words and claim held is already settled, so the GM's purpose (no rounds that fix nothing) is kept.

decisions.summary: T188: no change for building-review (error/questionable/nitpick/outside) or impl-drift (IN-STEP/DRIFTED/MISLABELED)
decisions.why: Taken one check at a time. Neither applies EDITs through make apply-edits. building-review is re-owed by the sheet's own fingerprint, and impl-drift by the code's and claims' fingerprints. A record or pop-up wording EDIT, the cascade the GM described ('a page edit re-owes checks on every pop-up citing it'), moves neither fingerprint, so the rule has nothing there to act on. The plan does not narrow the rule here: the cascade it targets does not pass through these checks.

decisions.summary: T188: only modal-depiction's contract gains a category in its EDIT header; every other check is one class throughout
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for telling modal-depiction's mixed classes apart. For every other check, the check's name already says its class.

decisions.summary: T189: a later round's bundle gains 'The change since round <n>', which pairs every changed run of lines since what the last round was bundled (EDITs and hand edits alike). The instruction is to judge only whether the change made something wrong, and the whole unit stays for context
decisions.why: This is 're-reviews scoped to the change'. Including hand edits makes the pairing complete rather than narrow. The scope reaches the reviewer as an instruction: what a reviewer judges cannot be enforced mechanically, and the 11-19 'real enforcement' approval was about the six improvements' guards. The mechanical part, the paired change in the bundle, is built.

decisions.summary: T189: a subject whose last round was bundled before the keeping gets no change section and reads the whole unit unscoped, as before
decisions.why: A transitional carve-out from 'scoped to the change'. What such a round was handed was never kept (the plan's premise: the bundle is overwritten on regeneration, and uncommitted EDITs and hand edits are not in git), so 'every change since the last round' cannot be paired for it. Telling a reviewer to judge ONLY a pairing that might miss a change would let an unpaired claim change through unreviewed, which defeats the GM's sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. The carve-out ends by itself: that round writes the kept bundle, so each subject is scoped from its next round on.

decisions.summary: T190: apply_edits/settled.rs refuses, before applying anything, an EDIT whose new text is an earlier round's EDIT's old text and whose old text is that EDIT's new text
decisions.why: This is 'settled choices stay settled' for the review rounds' oscillation that the GM raised under 'On oscillation and review scope'. It is a real refusal with a red-first test (the refusal off: failed).

decisions.summary: T190: the refusal uses the exact put-back test; the looser near_reversal (two content words back) stays a mark
decisions.why: Measured on 2026-11-23 over 1,670 EDITs: 3 were exact put-backs, and the loose test named 17 more that read as factual rounds widening a sentence. Refusing on the loose test would block factual corrections, which defeats the purpose the GM gave ('we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'). The near cases remain visible as marks.

decisions.summary: T190: a put-back is let through only when its finding carries 'REVERSES round <n>:' and an 'evidence:' quoting the words or naming the page, and its check's category is factual. A wording put-back has no way through
decisions.why: An exception to 'settled choices stay settled', taken on its own. Refusing every put-back of a settled fact would lock in a factual error that an earlier round introduced, which defeats the GM's stated purpose (fixing real flaws, factual inaccuracies). Requiring the stated error and its evidence keeps settled wording settled and allows no escape for style. FR-012's escape requirement covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this one, so leaving wording without an escape conflicts with no requirement.

decisions.summary: T190 (found and left): no refusal on the Edit tool for hand put-backs
decisions.why: Judged on the replay alone, case by case, not on the cited reversal:<file> rulings, which the bundle does not carry. In 24 of the 25 measured Edit-tool A->B->A put-backs a builder was revising its own code with no round between: nothing was settled. In the 1 (no_poll_hooks.rs) spec-fidelity replies came between, but no check's EDIT was involved: a spec review settles no code wording. The GM's rule sits under 'oscillation and review scope', that is, rounds undoing rounds, and that is refused at apply-edits. A hand edit of a record page is not a round's choice, and T189 still hands it to the next round as a paired change to judge.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: filed as [perf] tasks; the saving is stated as a floor of 84 of 115 wording-only later rounds, and the rest is a GUESS to be measured after landing
decisions.why: FR-013 counts the builders' loop and review rounds as performance work. The figures carry their date and method, and the unmeasured part is labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: Apply T186's pop-up change filter (clears, echo rule, ABSENCE arm) to the claims triage, so a page or procedure-section edit re-owes only the claims whose text it changed in a claim-bearing way; a generated doc's claims are touched only by rows whose text changed in words they repeat.
decisions.why: The GM's convergence talk approved 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and 're-reviews scoped to the change' ('Please do all of that'); the observed 73-claims-for-one-row re-owe is the cascade the GM said must be fixed before anything else.

decisions.summary: T186's page_change split in triage/change.rs; blocks_change shared by both triages rather than copied; md_words reads a procedure section's Markdown as page words so markup edits pair equal.
decisions.why: Implementation of D1; the same rule as the pop-ups, which is what the GM approved.

decisions.summary: Each changed page/section paired once, then judged per claim by change::fires with the claim's label and account as reader (question paths left out); no note key is a claim's, so the keys-gone arm never fires.
decisions.why: Applies T186's rule to the claim as its reader; the keys-gone arm not firing is a consequence of claims carrying no note keys, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Add change::echo_rewritten: the echo also read from a rewrite's new side, because a relabel rewrites a fact in words the claim repeats; without it the replay missed one DRIFTED claim.
decisions.why: Widens what is sent to the agent, so it narrows nothing; it keeps factual/label changes cascading as the GM's 'only factual findings cascade' intends.

decisions.summary: A claim whose every text edit is cleared, with no code hunk and nothing forced, is recorded cleared by the tool (record_cleared) with snapshots before skip/all-forced/dispatch paths run on the rest; the dispatch is skipped when nothing is left.
decisions.why: This is the 'cost no agent' outcome the GM asked for; code-hunk and forced claims still go on, and the quotation ruling (an original-language edit is never cleared) is kept.

decisions.summary: The claims-triage contract and MANIFEST form are unchanged; the MANIFEST shows only blocks left after the clears.
decisions.why: Scopes the remaining review to the change, as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: claims triage-replay --out DIR: a read-only replay of each owed claim's fate, used as the red-first and 0-misses measurement over today's landings.
decisions.why: Verification that the requested filter does what was asked (no DRIFTED claim whose drift lay in its own text is dropped); enforcement of the request, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Green exit stated as 0 misses of DRIFTED claims whose drift lay in the text they rest on; the two DRIFTED claims the tool clears are the known 'tax archive strongroom role' (its DRIFTED row kept) and 'main gate posts', reached only by an unrelated cart-gate edit of its section.
decisions.why: Clearing a claim on an edit that does not touch what it rests on is exactly the GM's rule ('the ones that never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade'); the measure matches the GM's rule rather than narrowing it. Both are named, and the known drift's verdict stands.

decisions.id: D9 left: main gate posts cites no page
decisions.summary: Leave the claims-grammar class (a CONVENTION claim whose figure a page states but which cites no page) to the claims grammar; the one instance was already restated at d4da911203.
decisions.why: Not something this request or T191 asks for (cascade scoping, not citation coverage); its one instance's wrong outcome is already fixed, so no wrong outcome is left by this task. Aside for the GM: worth a filed observation if other such claims are measured.

decisions.summary: PAIR_RATIO and ABSENCE stay T186's; function-word trigrams ('one of the') still count, sending 2 extra claims at the garden landing.
decisions.why: Over-sending two claims to an agent is no wrong outcome; leaving T186's approved rule as it is narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D11 rustfmt fix of T187's file
decisions.summary: Fix formatting only in rust/gate/crates/owed/src/item_relabel.rs, whose rustfmt failure turned the owed crate's make static red.
decisions.why: A tool refusing valid work is a defect fixed as found; formatting only, no behavior change. (It departs from the plan's own 'T187's files untouched' constraint, which is the coordinator's, not the GM's.)

decisions.summary: Classed as performance work: removes agent work before dispatch; no engine code, no map change; not a defect fix.
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM's 'prioritize performance improvements'; the work removed is agent time, the GM's stated cost.

decisions.summary: page_words drops every well-formed item tag (a malformed one stays visible), so a tag-only page edit owes no pop-up triage
decisions.why: The task's own goal (tagging owes no check) and the GM's approved convergence rules (labels are data and propagate by regeneration; only a claim-changing edit triggers review). A tag adds nothing a reader meets.

decisions.summary: a pop-up's {NNNN#id} reference is filled from its tag's data-guess whatever the label, resolved as the registry does (own question first, else the one other question tagging the id); verbatim reference owes nothing, a reworded data-guess owes the pop-up its checks, a relabel owes nothing
decisions.why: Serves 'tag the rest of the record' and the approved rules: only a claim-changing edit cascades, labels propagate mechanically. A rewording still owes checks, so nothing a reader sees escapes review.

decisions.summary: tag.py matched bullets to GUESS blocks at >=0.6 content-word overlap and placed fixed-form convention/deviation tags; 36 page sessions confirmed them
decisions.why: Method of carrying out the request; run before the GM approved the cheap route and kept, its results confirmed by sessions.

decisions.summary: cheap.py tags each remaining block that names its own label with an id and label and no bullet (476 GUESS, 32 CONVENTION, 27 DEVIATION); sessions only for the 9 blocks the script could not decide
decisions.why: Exactly the route the GM approved 2026-11-23: 'a script tags each block that names its own label ... only truly ambiguous blocks go to a session' - 'please proceed with that as the way forward'.

decisions.summary: the page check no longer requires a GUESS tag's data-guess; the registry refuses a reference to a GUESS tag without one, naming the fix (the referencing pop-up's author writes it from the block)
decisions.why: The GM's approved route verbatim: 'a Guesses sentence is written only when a pop-up first cites the item'. The registry refusal is enforcement of that clause, not new scope.

decisions.summary: the 100 attested blocks stay untagged until a claim names one, because nothing reads an ATTESTED tag except a claim naming the item and no classed claim anchored here names one
decisions.why: Narrows 'tag the rest of the record', but the exception is in the GM's own approval of the route: 'attested blocks are skipped if nothing reads their tags'. The plan measures that condition rather than assuming it (every reader of an item tag in rust/ read; grep of ATTESTED over rust/; an untagged block reads as unknown, never attested; the registry drops a non-GUESS reference), so the GM's condition is shown met, not completed on his behalf.

decisions.summary: T187's grammar is changed so one block may hold a GUESS tag beside a CONVENTION or DEVIATION tag, each needing its own word in the block (27 blocks on 22 pages)
decisions.why: Widens rather than narrows: under T187's rule those findings the GM asked tagged could not be tagged at all. Each tag must still match a word in its block (constitution XII: a tag never says more than its block).

decisions.summary: of the 9 blocks sent to sessions (negated or back-referring label words, nested-list blocks), 7 were tagged
decisions.why: The sessions are the GM's 'truly ambiguous blocks go to a session'; a block a session reads as stating no label (e.g. a negated convention word) has no label to tag, so leaving it is the goal met, not narrowed.

decisions.summary: an opus judge read the 94 classed claims still unanchored against their page's same-label tags; 72 now name their item; 22 cite a page where no tagged block states their decision and are left, listed in claims-verdicts.json; plain claims are not anchored
decisions.why: The goal is that claims on a tagged item name it; the 22 rest on no tagged item, so there is nothing to name, and plain claims carry no label for the tags to hold. Whether any of the 22 is itself a research defect is not shown by the plan; nothing here establishes one, and they are listed for reading.

decisions.summary: question_size counts an item tag for nothing
decisions.why: A tag is not prose; without this, tagging put 0196 over its cap and would have owed a split or a trim, contrary to the GM's rule that no size edit is ever substantive and to the goal that tagging owes no check.

decisions.summary: three found defects (relabeled_only impl-drift on anchored classed claims; refs.rs filling from its own question only; a dangling research pointer in registry tests) are each fixed in this task or by T200/T204, landed with its code
decisions.why: Each known defect is fixed before the step ends, as the fix-as-we-go rule asks; none is deferred.

decisions.summary: the strip and filled references land before or with the first tag batch; claims' anchors after T204; the whole bulk lands before the port resumes
decisions.why: The GM's condition 'tag the rest of the record before resuming our port'.

decisions.summary: the task is classed performance work
decisions.why: A scheduling class under FR-013; the task removes triages and pop-up checks a tag would have owed, and it is ordered before the port as the GM asked either way.

decisions.summary: A builder of a still-open task that the session reads as running is STALLED when it has no live work (listed in the Stop's background_tasks, a run or sub-agent its transcript launched, a sub-agent of its own writing within the bound) and its transcript (mtime) has not moved within STALL_SECS.
decisions.why: Anchored in the 2026-11-23 request: a check that is silent while the session is active or waiting on a tracked agent, and speaks only when it is idle with actionable work. A builder with no live work and a silent transcript is not a tracked wait, and it is actionable. The task line and brief the block cites are not in the bundle, so this is not checked against them.

decisions.summary: A builder is the session's own dispatch whose description opens with a feature number.
decisions.why: FR-006's builder is an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; this is that definition made readable.

decisions.summary: idle_check waits on every main-session Stop, not only one with an empty list, and names stalled builders when the session did not turn.
decisions.why: T184's builder went unnamed because every Stop listed a run except one, which returned at the hold. Waiting on every Stop is what lets the 2026-11-23 check speak when the session is idle with actionable work. It stays silent when the session turns, as T183 does.

decisions.summary: Stalled builders are named ahead of the hold and the open-task block; a hold holds new tasks, not a started builder's wake.
decisions.why: Two cases, ruled separately. (a) A hold on new tasks: the arbiter's ruling says '451 starts no new task', and waking a builder already started on an open task starts none, so the check still respects the binding ruling the 2026-11-23 request names. (b) A set-down of the builder's own task: the block decides nothing to override one. It names only a builder the session reads as still running, with no final notice and its task open in tasks.md, and it gives the wake command as information, not a block that compels it. The block has no explicit exclusion of a set-down task's builder, so that edge is flagged to the caller, not ruled as a narrowing the plan makes.

decisions.summary: Each stalled builder is named once while its last line is unchanged (once key 'stalled <id>').
decisions.why: T183's said-once rule and the GM's 2026-11-23 aim that the check add nothing to the context it need not.

decisions.summary: With no background_tasks list (a harness from before the field), no builder is named.
decisions.why: Without the list the check cannot tell whether a run the builder launched is still live. Naming would break the goal 'one at work is never named' and the GM's silent-while-waiting-on-a-tracked-agent rule, so the general rule is impossible here, not just awkward. It also covers only a harness that lacks the field, not today's case.

decisions.summary: LAUNCHED reads a Monitor's launch result ({taskId, timeoutMs}).
decisions.why: A defect fix in the reading the stall rule depends on: an agent waiting on its own watch was read as having no work (214 results measured).

decisions.summary: The Stop's list is re-read after the wait and at each look. A shell entry is live while a process holds its output file on fd 1 or 2, or while a live process's command line holds its command (its longest quote-free run of at least 12 characters, a CONVENTION) for Monitors, whose stream is a pipe.
decisions.why: The re-read closes the gap where a watch ends after the Stop (the D12 counterfactual) and serves the task's goal directly. The Monitor reading keeps a working builder from being named.

decisions.summary: A shell whose command is too short to tell, a subagent entry, and any entry where /proc cannot be read are kept as listed (live), failing toward silence.
decisions.why: Taken one at a time. A subagent's turn ends with a notice to the session, which wakes it, so that case cannot become T184's unheard stall. With /proc unreadable, liveness cannot be read at all. A command too short to match cannot be told from other processes, and guessing either way would name working builders, which the goal forbids. In each case the rule cannot be applied, not merely applied awkwardly.

decisions.summary: A listed shell whose writer waits on a dead producer (finished_run_hooks' stale_waiters) is no live work and is named with its pid, file and TaskStop <id>.
decisions.why: A defect fix (the gap audit's item 1): a waiter that will never finish is exactly a watch that will never wake its agent, so it is the task's own case.

decisions.summary: The check looks again when a quiet builder crosses the bound, or every RECHECK_SECS (GUESS 60 s) while live work runs, until WAIT_SECS (= STALL_SECS, 600 s). The Idle hook timeout is raised 420 -> 960 s (a CONVENTION pinned by a test).
decisions.why: Needed to name within about ten minutes a builder that goes quiet after the Stop with no Stop after (the gap audit's item 2). The knobs are labeled GUESS or CONVENTION.

decisions.summary: A builder past the context cap is named for a fresh dispatch from its handoff, not a SendMessage; CAP_TOKENS moves to shared::context.
decisions.why: FR-006 refuses a SendMessage that resumes a builder past the threshold, so a notice naming that command would contradict the spec.

decisions.summary: make builder-status [TRANSCRIPT=] says each builder of an open task working or stalled, and each dead-producer waiter, by the idle check's own reading of the last Stop's kept list, re-read now.
decisions.why: An addition. Its only source is the block's quotation of the task line ('the coordinator's status of a builder comes from that probe'), and that line is not in the bundle's request.md. It reads the same state as the idle check and changes no behavior. It narrows nothing, so it carries no ruling, but it is not verified against the GM's words.

decisions.summary: STALL_SECS (L7R_STALL_SECS) is a GUESS of 600 s, about twice the longest measured silence of an agent at work (280.6 s).
decisions.why: A knob labeled GUESS and derived from measured gaps (280.6 s longest), so that a working agent is never named, which the 2026-11-23 request's silent-while-waiting rule requires. The brief the block cites for the GUESS is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: Two builders that had reported done, with an interim notice never followed by a final one, are named once each; telling them apart is left.
decisions.why: Not a defect: neither was working, so the goal 'one at work is never named' holds. Each is named once with its own last line saying it stopped, and an open task whose builder has stopped is something the session can act on. No wrong outcome is left.

decisions.summary: The idle check's words do not reach make guard-messages' corpus. They were judged by message-check on a hand-built bundle and its cuts applied; wiring the corpus is left.
decisions.why: The words the GM asked to have reviewed for brevity and fidelity were reviewed by that same check, so no unjudged output ships. The remaining gap is only that a later edit would not be caught automatically. Under constitution XIV v2.36.0 that is a check's reach with no wrong outcome today, not a defect, and leaving it changes nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: A builder whose live work outlasts WAIT_SECS, with the session silent and no later Stop, is not named. Filed as T201, to land before T200.
decisions.why: This is a deferred defect, and it meets FR-009's terms: it states why it is not fixed here, its filed task id and its order. The reason is real, not a matter of cost. The idle check can wake the session only by exiting under the hook entry's timeout, and Claude Code's cap on that timeout is unmeasured. Building a longer wait on a guessed cap risks the hook being killed and losing the case this task does cover. The project's rule is to measure such a number, not assume it. T184's own case, a watch ending within minutes of the Stop, is fixed here.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests in today's shape, the replay against today's real Stops, T184's files untouched, one landing.
decisions.why: Enforces and measures the task's own goal; nothing outside it.

blocks: ### T193 (the GM 2026-11-23, the task line; observed 2026-11-23: 451 T184's builder `a676c53072fd7258b` waited from 20:27:39Z to 21:35 on a watch that had ended, and the idle check said nothing)
### T193 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: A builder of a still-open task that the session reads as running is STALLED when it has no live work (listed in the Stop's background_tasks, a run or sub-agent its transcript launched, a sub-agent of its own writing within the bound) and its transcript (mtime) has not moved within STALL_SECS.
decisions.why: Anchored in the 2026-11-23 request: a check that is silent while the session is active or waiting on a tracked agent, and speaks only when it is idle with actionable work. A builder with no live work and a silent transcript is not a tracked wait, and it is actionable. The task line and brief the block cites are not in the bundle, so this is not checked against them.

decisions.summary: A builder is the session's own dispatch whose description opens with a feature number.
decisions.why: FR-006's builder is an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; this is that definition made readable.

decisions.summary: idle_check waits on every main-session Stop, not only one with an empty list, and names stalled builders when the session did not turn.
decisions.why: T184's builder went unnamed because every Stop listed a run except one, which returned at the hold. Waiting on every Stop is what lets the 2026-11-23 check speak when the session is idle with actionable work. It stays silent when the session turns, as T183 does.

decisions.summary: Stalled builders are named ahead of the hold and the open-task block; a hold holds new tasks, not a started builder's wake.
decisions.why: Two cases, ruled separately. (a) A hold on new tasks: the arbiter's ruling says '451 starts no new task', and waking a builder already started on an open task starts none, so the check still respects the binding ruling the 2026-11-23 request names. (b) A set-down of the builder's own task: the block decides nothing to override one. It names only a builder the session reads as still running, with no final notice and its task open in tasks.md, and it gives the wake command as information, not a block that compels it. The block has no explicit exclusion of a set-down task's builder, so that edge is flagged to the caller, not ruled as a narrowing the plan makes.

decisions.summary: Each stalled builder is named once while its last line is unchanged (once key 'stalled <id>').
decisions.why: T183's said-once rule and the GM's 2026-11-23 aim that the check add nothing to the context it need not.

decisions.summary: With no background_tasks list (a harness from before the field), no builder is named.
decisions.why: Without the list the check cannot tell whether a run the builder launched is still live. Naming would break the goal 'one at work is never named' and the GM's silent-while-waiting-on-a-tracked-agent rule, so the general rule is impossible here, not just awkward. It also covers only a harness that lacks the field, not today's case.

decisions.summary: LAUNCHED reads a Monitor's launch result ({taskId, timeoutMs}).
decisions.why: A defect fix in the reading the stall rule depends on: an agent waiting on its own watch was read as having no work (214 results measured).

decisions.summary: The Stop's list is re-read after the wait and at each look. A shell entry is live while a process holds its output file on fd 1 or 2, or while a live process's command line holds its command (its longest quote-free run of at least 12 characters, a CONVENTION) for Monitors, whose stream is a pipe.
decisions.why: The re-read closes the gap where a watch ends after the Stop (the D12 counterfactual) and serves the task's goal directly. The Monitor reading keeps a working builder from being named.

decisions.summary: A shell whose command is too short to tell, a subagent entry, and any entry where /proc cannot be read are kept as listed (live), failing toward silence.
decisions.why: Taken one at a time. A subagent's turn ends with a notice to the session, which wakes it, so that case cannot become T184's unheard stall. With /proc unreadable, liveness cannot be read at all. A command too short to match cannot be told from other processes, and guessing either way would name working builders, which the goal forbids. In each case the rule cannot be applied, not merely applied awkwardly.

decisions.summary: A listed shell whose writer waits on a dead producer (finished_run_hooks' stale_waiters) is no live work and is named with its pid, file and TaskStop <id>.
decisions.why: A defect fix (the gap audit's item 1): a waiter that will never finish is exactly a watch that will never wake its agent, so it is the task's own case.

decisions.summary: The check looks again when a quiet builder crosses the bound, or every RECHECK_SECS (GUESS 60 s) while live work runs, until WAIT_SECS (= STALL_SECS, 600 s). The Idle hook timeout is raised 420 -> 960 s (a CONVENTION pinned by a test).
decisions.why: Needed to name within about ten minutes a builder that goes quiet after the Stop with no Stop after (the gap audit's item 2). The knobs are labeled GUESS or CONVENTION.

decisions.summary: A builder past the context cap is named for a fresh dispatch from its handoff, not a SendMessage; CAP_TOKENS moves to shared::context.
decisions.why: FR-006 refuses a SendMessage that resumes a builder past the threshold, so a notice naming that command would contradict the spec.

decisions.summary: make builder-status [TRANSCRIPT=] says each builder of an open task working or stalled, and each dead-producer waiter, by the idle check's own reading of the last Stop's kept list, re-read now.
decisions.why: An addition. Its only source is the block's quotation of the task line ('the coordinator's status of a builder comes from that probe'), and that line is not in the bundle's request.md. It reads the same state as the idle check and changes no behavior. It narrows nothing, so it carries no ruling, but it is not verified against the GM's words.

decisions.summary: STALL_SECS (L7R_STALL_SECS) is a GUESS of 600 s, about twice the longest measured silence of an agent at work (280.6 s).
decisions.why: A knob labeled GUESS and derived from measured gaps (280.6 s longest), so that a working agent is never named, which the 2026-11-23 request's silent-while-waiting rule requires. The brief the block cites for the GUESS is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: Two builders that had reported done, with an interim notice never followed by a final one, are named once each; telling them apart is left.
decisions.why: Not a defect: neither was working, so the goal 'one at work is never named' holds. Each is named once with its own last line saying it stopped, and an open task whose builder has stopped is something the session can act on. No wrong outcome is left.

decisions.summary: The idle check's words do not reach make guard-messages' corpus. They were judged by message-check on a hand-built bundle and its cuts applied; wiring the corpus is left.
decisions.why: The words the GM asked to have reviewed for brevity and fidelity were reviewed by that same check, so no unjudged output ships. The remaining gap is only that a later edit would not be caught automatically. Under constitution XIV v2.36.0 that is a check's reach with no wrong outcome today, not a defect, and leaving it changes nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: A builder whose live work outlasts WAIT_SECS, with the session silent and no later Stop, is not named. Filed as T201, to land before T200.
decisions.why: This is a deferred defect, and it meets FR-009's terms: it states why it is not fixed here, its filed task id and its order. The reason is real, not a matter of cost. The idle check can wake the session only by exiting under the hook entry's timeout, and Claude Code's cap on that timeout is unmeasured. Building a longer wait on a guessed cap risks the hook being killed and losing the case this task does cover. The project's rule is to measure such a number, not assume it. T184's own case, a watch ending within minutes of the Stop, is fixed here.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests in today's shape, the replay against today's real Stops, T184's files untouched, one landing.
decisions.why: Enforces and measures the task's own goal; nothing outside it.
